subject: New levels for prediction in multilevel model

messages.author: 1457d345496c6c07
messages.subject: New levels for prediction in multilevel model
parts:
Hello all, 
I am using stan to fit a multilevel logistic regression model that includes random effects for age and period (year). I would like to be able to do a prediction for some new observations with observed patterns of the covariates in the model, but for a future period. So this is a type of forecast in a very loose sense of the word. My model is attached, and a link to my data is here:

https://drive.google.com/open?id=0B7G5045BmRHzQkRjUEgzc1p1UUk

In the generated quantities block, I do prediction for some new cases, but I can only include values of my variable `year_pred` that lie within the observed range. The data have year ranges of 1 to 14, but I would like to get a prediction for year 19 (posterior predicted value). If, otherwise stan throws an error: 

"accessing element out of range. index 19 out of range; expecting index to be between 1 and 15;"

I see that rstanarm has the capacity in its posterior_predict() function to include new levels of a group-level variable. My issue is that my model has an random walk term for one of the random effects that rstanarm can't handle. My question is, how can I get rstan to allow me to do this in the generated quantities block? Any suggestions would be appreciated.

-Corey

The data have year ranges of 1 to 14, but I would like to get a prediction for year 19 (posterior predicted value). If, otherwise stan throws an error:

I see that rstanarm has the capacity in its posterior_predict() function to include new levels of a group-level variable. My issue is that my model has an random walk term for one of the random effects that rstanarm can't handle. My question is, how can I get rstan to allow me to do this in the generated quantities block? Any suggestions would be appreciated.

You have to walk the age-specific parameter forward 5 periods and then form the linear predictor, success probability, and realization from the Bernoulli distribution. Something like
a1_15 <- normal_rng(a1[14], sigma_a1);
a1_16 <- normal_rng(a1_15, sigma_a1);
a1_17 <- normal_rng(a1_16, sigma_a1);
a1_18 <- normal_rng(a1_17, sigma_a1);
a1_19 <- normal_rng(a1_18, sigma_a1);
y_pred[i] <- bernoulli_rng(inv_logit(...));

Ben
